subject: Post-call: Helix privacy needs — audit log exports, PII scope, and delivery options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Helix privacy needs — audit log exports, PII scope, and delivery options

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Alyssa — good to meet you and the team. Quick recap and requests so we can size the deliverable and timeline:  

- Ask: Helix needs an audit evidence bundle for onboarding / procurement review that demonstrates who accessed customer data (who/when), the object accessed (call id or resource id), and the action performed (read/generate/delete).
- Retention: You mentioned legally required retention of access logs for 2 years, with 90-day hot access for incident response.
- PII scope: You indicated names, MRN-like identifiers, and free-text clinical notes may be present and need redaction guidance.
- Format preferences: You flagged CSV exports for legal, plus Parquet for analytics.

What we need from you to produce a scoped sample export:  
1) Confirm the time range you want in the sample (recommended: 30 days) and timezone to use for timestamps.
2) Confirm whether Helix requires pseudonymization (hashing) of identifiers in the sample or redaction of free-text.
3) Any particular columns you'd like in the who/when report beyond: timestamp, user_email, user_role, resource_id, action, session_id, ip_address, request_id.

Next steps: once you confirm the bullets above, Marissa (CC) will put together a small sample slice (CSV + Parquet stub) and a short runbook describing our collection points and retention policy. We can also provide a hashed-identifier version and a redacted free-text sample so your legal team can verify.  

Attachments I plan to include in the sample package: who_when_sample.csv (schema only), export_schema_stub.pdf, and a redaction-policy-v1.docx.

If it's helpful, please loop in your security contact or legal review email and we can route the artifacts directly to them.  

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

From: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@helixhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Health Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix privacy needs — audit log exports, PII scope, and delivery options

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline:  

- Time range for sample: 30 days is perfect, please use 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30 for consistency with our procurement packet. Timestamps should be in UTC.
- Pseudonymization: Legal prefers anonymized identifiers in samples (SHA-256 hash of MRN), but they want one unaudited sample with masked names (first initial + last name) to validate field mapping.
- Columns: please include an extra column "resource_type" (e.g., "conversation", "embedding", "attachment") and "action_detail" free text for context.

Retention: Helix policy requires 2 years of retention, and audit exports must be exportable as compressed Parquet with a manifest CSV. Requests for logs during review are typically for a 30‑90 day window, but we store 2 years.

Delivery: We will need a signed DPA addendum before you share any sample with live identifiers (even hashed). Can you send a DocuSign link for the DPA? Also: turnaround expectation is 3 business days for the sample after we sign.

Alyssa
Sr. PM, Privacy & Integrations
Helix Health
alyssa@helixhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix privacy needs — audit log exports, PII scope, and delivery options

Alyssa — thanks, noted. A couple of technical clarifications from our side:  

1) Export content and formats
   - We can produce both compressed Parquet (preferred for analytics) and canonical CSV. The delivery package will include a small manifest CSV that lists files, record counts, and SHA256 checksums.
   - For parity with your legal ask, we'll provide two variants of the sample: (A) hashed identifiers (SHA-256 with salt) and (B) masked-display (first initial + last name) for mapping.

2) Timestamps and timezone
   - We'll normalize all timestamps to UTC and include an offset_ts column in the manifest for auditability. We'll also include both event_time_utc and event_time_epoch for your parsing team.

3) PII redaction approach and free-text
   - For free-text notes we can (i) redact PHI entities using our named-entity redaction pipeline, (ii) provide a redaction log with line numbers, or (iii) deliver a pseudo-tokenized version where identifiable tokens are replaced with stable pseudonyms. Which do you prefer for the sample?

4) Access controls proof
   - We can include a short runbook and sample IAM/log queries (example: SELECT FROM audit WHERE action='read' AND timestamp BETWEEN ...) and a minimal RBAC matrix export.

Karthik — assigning to you to assemble the sample files and the manifest. Please produce: who_when_sample.csv (schema + 30-row sample), who_when_sample.parquet (schema stub), export_manifest.csv, and redaction-policy-v1.docx. Keep the hashed-salt private; only hashed outputs in the sample.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: who_when_sample.csv (CSV, schema only)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Helix Health Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix privacy needs — audit log exports, PII scope, and delivery options

Thanks all — putting expected timeline on record:  

- Today (Thu): we send DocuSign DPA addendum link for review.
- After signed DPA (ETA 1 business day): Karthik will drop the sample package (CSV + Parquet + manifest + redaction-runbook) within 3 business days.
- We'll label the package with the date range 2026-09-01_to_2026-09-30 and include the two identifier variants (hashed and masked).

Alyssa — DocuSign link is below. Please confirm who on legal will sign so we can set the routing order. If Helix prefers we can also provide a short static sample to legal that contains only schema (no hashed values) while the DPA is routing.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/ABCDEF-Helix-DPA
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/HLX-2026-089

I'll follow up once the DPA is out.

—Jordan

From: Helix Health Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helix privacy needs — audit log exports, PII scope, and delivery options

Jordan/Marissa — legal has reviewed. We will:  

1) Sign the DPA addendum (routing to our VP Legal). Expect completed routing by end of business day tomorrow.
2) Please provide the schema-only sample package immediately (no hashed or masked values) so we can validate column mapping with our data team while DPA routes.
3) After DPA completes we will accept the hashed sample (SHA-256) and the masked-display sample for verification.

For the schema-only package please include a small README describing the manifest fields and the salt policy (we don't need the salt, just the fact that one is used). Also: include a timezone note stating all timestamps are UTC.

Thanks — Carla Ramos
VP Legal Operations
Helix Health
[Attachment: legal_review_checklist.pdf (referenced)]
